reason: The two affinity modules faithfully prove the printed separate-coordinate affinity property as MvPolynomial.degreeOf z≤1 for every actual scalar coordinate z. I inspected the definitions, expanded polynomial identities, all endpoint cases and the compiled public statements. The Δ result needs no extra premise and therefore covers all printed distinct triples. The T result requires exactly the three pairwise-remoteness hypotheses and no Generic, nonzero-value or coordinate-dependence condition. These are full-ring polynomial degree bounds, not statements merely about numerical evaluations or total degree.
mathematical_justification: Every mixed monomial coordinateX i * coordinateY j contains at most one occurrence of any scalar variable z because scalar indices are vertex labels paired with distinct Fin-2 component labels. Exhausting the two scalar components proves the bound even when i=j. The reversed product follows by commutativity. Sums and differences preserve a bound of one by the maximum-degree inequalities; cancellation may lower degree but cannot invalidate the bound.

The exact six-term areaPolynomial_expanded identity cancels the base x_i*y_i and y_i*x_i terms. Every remaining term is a mixed x/y monomial with signs matching det(P_j−P_i,P_k−P_i). Applying the mixed-monomial and add/subtract bounds proves areaPolynomial_affine for every scalar coordinate and every triple. No assumption about actual dependence or nonzeroness is used.

The actual line-row entries −d_y and d_x are differences of single coordinates. linePolynomialC_eq_free proves cancellation of the self terms in det(μ_e,d_e), leaving x_e*y_(e+1)−y_e*x_(e+1). This exact identity gives the same separate-coordinate degree bound for C. Exhausting Fin 3 covers all row entries. If z’s vertex label is neither endpoint of the edge, the inspected variable-support proof shows z is absent from the row entry, hence has degree zero there.

For a product of one entry from each of three remote edge rows, the proof splits exhaustively according to whether z’s vertex belongs to edge e, then edge f. In the first case endpoint separation forces both f and g row degrees to zero; in the second it forces e and g to zero; in the remaining case e and f are zero and the g bound is at most one. Coordinates outside all three rows are included. Combining the two multiplication-degree inequalities in each case proves the triple product bound without assuming the entries or their product are nonzero.

The actual six-term 3×3 determinant formula uses one row entry from e, f and g in every signed term. The proved triple-product bound therefore applies to all six terms, and the add/subtract inequalities yield concurrencePolynomial_affine. Pairwise-remoteness is the precise source condition supplying disjoint endpoint supports; no stronger index-separation or regularity hypothesis is added.

The resulting degree≤1 statements cover the printed affinity property, including unused coordinates and zero special cases. This review does not infer the later explicit a*x+b representation over a remaining-variable ring, nonzero slope from genuine dependence, or resultant/root certificates; those are separate remaining obligations. The independently compiled trace confirms the exact types and axiom sets.
